memory_candidates.content: An extension can exist fully in an agent-system source store (agent-system/extensions/<name>/) with a complete manifest.json, scripts, and context tree, yet never have been loaded into a given host's .claude-extensions.json -- meaning NONE of its files have ever reached .claude/**, even though tasks routinely research/plan/implement against its task_type. Before a redeploy step in any task that touches a source-store extension, check .claude-extensions.json's active extensions list explicitly (python3 -c "import json; print(list(json.load(open('.claude-extensions.json'))['extensions'].keys()))") rather than assuming deploy-headless.sh's default (non-destructive resync of already-active extensions only) will pick up a never-loaded one. If it is missing, load it first via a headless nvim call to manager.load('<name>', {confirm=false, project_dir=<repo>}) (mirroring deploy-headless.sh's own bootstrap-core call shape) before the normal deploy-headless.sh resync -- this is additive only and never destructive to other extensions.

An extension's manifest.json can declare a provides.context category (e.g. "contracts") that legitimately OVERRIDES a same-path core context file once the extension loads after core -- this is by design, not drift. verify-deploy.sh's manifest-driven content-hash check (item 5, verify.lua) is NOT override-aware: it attributes any content difference from core's own source to a core defect, even when the deployed content correctly reflects a later-loaded extension's intentional override. When this check fires with "core: Content differs from source" for a path also present in another loaded extension's own context tree, check `grep -rl "<distinguishing header text>" agent-system/extensions/*/context/**/*.md` before assuming it is a real drift -- it may be a legitimate override the checker cannot distinguish from a stale copy.
